query: The Supper Hatch {The kitchen hatch shuts at the bell, and the bell is going, and you are at the wrong end of the longest hall in the castle.|The hatch is coming down again. The cook leaves it open an inch less for you every week, on principle.|You hear the hatch rattle before you're through the door. Stew night, too.} Run the length of the hall {You get a bowl under the hatch as it comes down. The cook gives you the last of the stew and a look of grudging respect.|You make it with a slide that would win prizes. The hatch stops for you. The cook looks almost impressed.|In under the shutter by a hand's breadth. The cook says, "You again," and adds a dumpling, as a prize.} {The hatch closes in your face, gently, with finality. Bread and cheese it is.|You slip on the flagstones halfway and arrive on your back. The cook leans over the hatch to check you're alive, and closes it.|Too slow. You hear the stew being scraped into a bucket for the pigs, which is a sound that stays with you.} Take bread and cheese from the board {You take bread and cheese from the board by the door and eat them on the steps. It's fine. It isn't stew.|Bread, cheese and an apple, eaten walking. You catch the smell of the stew all the way upstairs.|You take the board's bread and somebody's abandoned pudding. You're not proud. You're full.} Cross the hall in a heartbeat {You're at the hatch before the bell's first echo. The cook stares at the door, then at you, then ladles. "Well," she says. "Somebody's hungry."|Haste down the long aisle, between the benches, round a prefect, and your bowl is under the hatch with time to spare.|You arrive so fast you have to wait for the hatch to finish opening. The cook gives you seconds out of sheer surprise.}
